clue.text: Important person of considerable size — former politician, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound of a word is wanted rather than its spelling

parts.note: a Whig belonged to a historic British party, superseded by the Liberals

explanation.surface: A description of a hefty retired politician who still carries weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were an 18th-19th century British party, hence 'former'; the word sounds the same as the hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is an informal term for someone of high rank or influence.

clue.text: Defender unhappy to admit defeat

parts.note: a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A dejected footballer reluctantly concedes the match is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is an idiom for withdrawing from a position or conceding.

clue.text: Greek getting close to one magnificent French city

parts.note: Gr is the abbreviation for Greek

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A Greek visitor nearing a splendid French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as nearby, but it means the end of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps.

clue.text: One mostly dark house

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A description of a single gloomy dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' is an adjective in the surface but stands for the noun gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit dwelling built of snow blocks, so a kind of house.

clue.text: He gets in new bedding material

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man climbs into freshly made bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheeting is fabric used for making bed linen, a material for bedding.

clue.text: Moving direction during trial

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a hearing is a court trial
a trend is a general direction

explanation.surface: A dramatic change of direction in the middle of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like motion, matching 'direction', but means emotionally affecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-rending causes deep sorrow, which is what moving means emotionally.

clue.text: Show form

definitions.meaning: second meaning: set up or found

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns (a show, a form), but each is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact is to prove it, and to establish a company is to found it.

clue.text: Disregard poor region

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are put in a different state

explanation.surface: An instruction to overlook a deprived area.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay no attention to it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: First of galleons, say, in Channel?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: Spanish galleons sailing the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' with galleons calls up the English Channel; the question mark flags a humbler channel, for rainwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a channel along a roof or street that carries away water.

clue.text: Almost all in team love the French language

indicators.note: almost all of something stops just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A team bonding over a shared love of France and its language.
explanation.definitionFit: A creole is a language formed from a mix of others, becoming a community's mother tongue.

clue.text: Woman, teacher originally, is a strict disciplinarian

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A female teacher with a reputation for keeping order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' just means a woman's name here, so any name could be meant until the letters narrow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is someone who insists on rigid obedience, named after a 17th-century French drillmaster.

clue.text: Crazy about port with desserts

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: Split is a port on Croatia's Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: Someone mad about port wine served alongside puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy about' reads as one phrase meaning keen on, but 'about' is the wrapping signal; 'port' suggests the drink, yet it is Split on Croatia's Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is an ice-cream dessert served on a halved banana.

clue.text: Antiperspirant, too darned smelly!

indicators.note: something smelly is off or rotten, so these letters are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint that an antiperspirant has far too strong a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiperspirants are commonly sold combined with, and called, deodorants; the definition is loose but standard.

clue.text: Good aboard simple canal boat

indicators.note: something aboard is on a ship, carried inside it

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Praise for a plain, unfussy narrowboat on the canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed boat built for carrying goods along canals.

clue.text: Dish was terrible when dished out round hospital

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the mixed letters wrap about another piece
food dished out is served around and spread about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A complaint about awful hospital food being served up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' and 'dished out' sit together to make the clue feel about food throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, cheese sauce on toast, is a savoury dish.

clue.text: Handle snake that's got inside very warm vessel

indicators.note: having got inside means sitting within, so these pieces go in the middle of another

parts.note: to handle a tool is to use it
a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.surface: A warning about a snake that has slipped into a hot container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a pot to match 'very warm'; it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a boat fitted out as a home, and a vessel is any craft afloat.

clue.text: Landlord's widely known — a name

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A landlord whose name is famous far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: The landlord here runs a British pub, not a property lettings business.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican is the keeper of a pub, commonly called its landlord in Britain.

clue.text: Before completion of repair, insert a different filter

indicators.note: before fixes the order, so the reworked letters come ahead of the final one
different means changed, so the letters take a new arrangement
the completion of a word is where it ends, so only its last letter counts

explanation.surface: A plumber's instruction to fit a new filter before finishing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve or filter that holds back solids while liquid passes through.

clue.text: Cunning stunt hurt cad in aggressive competition

indicators.note: a cunning scheme is artfully contrived, so these letters are rearranged craftily

explanation.surface: A rogue gets injured by a crafty trick during a fierce contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and thrust is an idiom from swordplay for lively, combative rivalry or debate.

clue.text: Wager about minister getting a military commission

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman places a bet on securing an army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A brevet was a commission giving an officer a higher nominal rank without the extra pay.

clue.text: Ring cleric for a change

indicators.note: a change means altering things, so the letters are swapped round

explanation.surface: A suggestion to phone a different priest than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like an instruction to phone; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a round shape, which is what a circle is.

clue.text: Put up beams, noisily

indicators.note: noisily means out loud, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

explanation.surface: Builders hoisting roof timbers with a lot of clatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' suggests timbers to put up, but here they are beams of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it or set it up in a higher position.

clue.text: Secretary brings in an order holding a cigar

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: holding here just puts the single letter alongside, keeping it within the enclosed group

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

explanation.surface: An office assistant passes round a request for a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' tempts as a religious or honours order, but it is the verb, to command; the secretary's two letters enclose everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long, slender cigar.

clue.text: Article on extremely mundane subject

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes of a word, so only its two outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of mundane

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a thoroughly dull topic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed beneath, so the article comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a piece of writing or talk.

clue.text: Girl falls in London station

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a major railway terminus in London

explanation.surface: A girl takes a tumble at a busy London terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' also nods to a third sense, the Victoria Falls on the Zambezi.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a common female forename and also that of a main-line London rail terminus.

clue.text: Minister in study, entertaining company after drop of alcohol

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a den is a private study

indicators.note: after fixes the order, placing the company abbreviation behind the single letter
a drop is a tiny amount, so just the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A clergyman at his desk, hosting visitors after a nip of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest in many churches.

clue.text: Pay for one's English paper

parts.note: to treat someone is to pay for them
I is the Roman numeral one, plus the 's
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone asking to be paid for an English newspaper or essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a newspaper but means a scholarly essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject, the academic sense of paper.

clue.text: Judge, note, having no time for physician

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: having no means going without, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A judge, noting he lacks time, sends for the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a musical note, but it is a banknote; a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Jenner was the English physician who pioneered smallpox vaccination.
